title: GPU Fleet Health: Annotated Vitals, Telemetry Mapping, and Alerting Matrix
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This document defines a standard mapping from raw GPU telemetry and host signals to a small set of annotated "vitals" used for health judgement, alerting, dashboarding, and automated operational actions for the Redwood GPU fleet. The goal is to make GPU health signals consistent across providers and machine types, enable deterministic runbooks, and provide clear ownership boundaries for SRE and infra teams.

Why this exists
- GPU telemetry is noisy and vendor-specific; teams spend too much time translating signals during incidents.
- Consistent health annotations let higher layers (schedulers, autoscalers, runtime) make safe decisions: drain, prewarm, fall back to CPU, or route to alternate regions.
- This doc standardizes derived metric names, severity thresholds, sampling/aggregation windows, and the associated automatic remediation ladder.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to all GPU nodes in Redwood-managed fleets (hosted and Dedicated).
- Covers device-level telemetry (temperature, power, ECC), host-level signals (OOM kills, cgroup throttles, kernel messages), and derived invariants (thermal climb rate, error-rate-per-hour).
- Not a replacement for vendor firmware guides; ties those signals to our operational model.

Definitions (canonical terms)
- GPU_VITAL_THERMAL: derived single-value state representing thermal safety. One of: normal | warm | hot | critical. Computed from temperature and climb-rate.
- GPU_VITAL_ECC: ECC error classification: none | transient | persistent | fatal. Uses ECC counters and DDR parity logs.
- GPU_VITAL_POWER: power headroom state: normal | capped | unstable. Based on power draw and power-limit throttles.
- GPU_VITAL_MEM_PRESSURE: memory contention state: normal | fragmentation | OOM-risk. From free VRAM, allocation failure events, and fragmentation heuristics.
- GPU_VITAL_PREEMPT_SCORE: a 0..100 score indicating preemption risk (higher = more likely to preempt). Derived from preempt events, priority shares, and soft-quota usage.

Telemetry fields and mapping table
Use the following canonical metric names in Prometheus and the telemetry envelope. Vendors may export different field names; collectors must map vendor IDs to these canonical names at ingestion.

| Canonical metric | Typical sources | Aggregation window | Notes / derived use |
|------------------|-----------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| gpu.temp_celsius | nvidia_smi.temperature.gpu, amd_gpu.temp | 30s -> 1m | Use instantaneous and 1m rolling mean for climb-rate calculation. |
| gpu.temp_climb_c_per_min | derived | 60s -> 5m | 1m delta extrapolated to per-minute rate; important for hot transitions. |
| gpu.ecc.corrected_count | nvidia_smi.ecc.corrected | 5m | Convert to errors/hour metric; transient vs persistent rule below. |
| gpu.ecc.uncorrectable_count | vendor | 5m | Immediate critical if >0 AND not from NVLink retry storms. |
| gpu.power_w | nvml.power | 30s | Track against configured TDP and observed power cap throttles. |
| gpu.power_limit_throttle | nvml.power.limit_throttled | 1m | Binary flag used in GPU_VITAL_POWER. |
| gpu.vram_free_mb | nvml.memory.free | 30s -> 1m | Use percentile (p5, p50) over 5m for OOM risk. |
| node.oom_kills | kernel.oom | 1m | If OOM occurs on a node with active GPU workloads, escalate to persistent memory issues. |
| node.cgroup_throttle_count | cgroup.v2.io.throttled | 1m | Correlate with preempt_score and slow-path fallbacks. |
| pci.link_errors | kernel.pci.link_errors | 5m | High-rate link errors influence ECC and fatal classifications. |
| gpu.utilization_pct | nvml.utilization.gpu | 30s | Used for autoscaler and scheduling heuristics. |
| gpu.driver_recoveries | vendor | 1m | Count of recoveries / GPU resets; 3 in 10m -> persistent fault. |

Severity thresholds and derived rules
The following table is the canonical severity matrix used by alerting rules. Rules should use the aggregation windows above and apply deduplication across sources for the same host.

| Vital | Transition condition | Alert severity | Automated action |
|-------|---------------------|----------------|------------------|
| GPU_VITAL_THERMAL: warm -> normal | temp_celsius between 70-80C and climb_rate < 5 C/min | info | log to fleet metrics, no remediation |
| warm -> hot | temp >= 80C OR climb_rate >= 5 C/min | warning | reduce tenant concurrency on node; notify owner_team |
| hot -> critical | temp >= 90C OR sustained climb_rate >= 10 C/min | critical | initiate graceful drain with 10s token window, trigger preemptible fallback routing |
| GPU_VITAL_ECC: transient | corrected_count spikes > 100/hour but no driver_recoveries | warning | increase ECC sampling, tag node for observation for 6h |
| ECC persistent | corrected_count persists > 10/hour for 24h OR 1 uncorrectable_count | critical | schedule urgent maintenance, remove node from allocator until sign-off |
| GPU_VITAL_POWER: capped | power_limit_throttle observed 3x in 5m | warning | reduce batch sizes for new sessions, notify infra team |
| GPU_VITAL_MEM_PRESSURE: OOM-risk | vram_free_mb p5 < 200MB OR node.oom_kills > 0 | critical | prevent new allocations, drain long-running low-priority sessions |

Behavioral guidelines for derived states
- Do not take the node off rotation for a single transient metric spike; require 3 observations across 2 minutes unless the metric is explicitly fatal (e.g. uncorrectable ECC).
- Combine signals: an isolated temperature spike with no climb-rate and no driver_recoveries = informational. Temperature + climb + driver_recovery = critical.
- Prefers graceful draining over immediate VM termination. Draining: mark as DRAINING, allow up to X=10s for active generation tokens to finish; after that attempt cancellation and eviction.

Alerting and runbook mapping
- Alerts are categorized and routed using the canonical vital name in the alert label (alert:gpu_vital_thermal, gpu_vital_ecc, etc.).
- Each alert must include: node_id, instance_type, model_variants_active (top-3 by qps), recent_driver_recoveries, and last_3_temp_samples.

Minimal runbook (summary)
1) Acknowledge within SLO: 5 minutes for warning, 2 minutes for critical.
2) Quickly determine if the node is in a multi-node tenant pool or dedicated to a single tenant.
3) For thermal warning: reduce concurrency -> monitor temperature; if climbs continue escalate to critical.
4) For ECC persistent or driver_recovery storms: cordon node from scheduler immediately and schedule maintenance ticket (priority P1 for critical).
5) For OOM-risk: set node-prevent-new-allocations flag and migrate priority sessions.
6) Include a short post-incident run listing: timestamps of first detection, remediation start, drain completion, follow-up maintenance ticket id.

Sample PromQL rules (examples)
- Thermal critical alert (pseudo):
  max_over_time(gpu.temp_celsius[2m]) > 90 and increase(gpu.temp_climb_c_per_min[5m]) > 20
- ECC persistent:
  increase(gpu.ecc.corrected_count[24h]) > 240
- Driver recovery storm:
  increase(gpu.driver_recoveries[10m]) > 3

Telemetry ingestion and mapping responsibilities
- Collector teams must publish vendor-to-canonical mappings in a small config file (YAML) kept in the infra telemetry repo. Example mapping: vendor.nvml.temperature.gpu -> gpu.temp_celsius.
- Sampling: device-level metrics at 30s; host-level at 15s if the host is in a degraded state. Retention: raw samples 90d; rolled-up 1m aggregates for 1y.

Dashboard and SLOs
- Dashboards must expose the 90-day incidence rate of each critical vital per pool. Target: <0.5 critical thermal events per 100 nodes per 90 days for stable pools.
- SLOs for remediation: 95% of warning-class events should be acknowledged in 5 minutes and have an automated mitigation (concurrency reduction or drain) applied within 10 minutes.

Automated remediation ladder (preferred order)
1) Soft remediation: reduce tenant concurrency, lower batch sizes, and increase per-request CPU fallback ratio.
2) Scheduler-level: stop placing new jobs, mark node as_low_priority.
3) Drain: graceful drain window (10s) then force-evict if necessary.
4) Cordon and maintenance: mark node as out-of-service, create maintenance ticket tied to the telemetry snapshots.

Ownership and escalation
- First-line responder: infra-gpu-oncall (team: eng-infra SRE rotation).
- Secondary: hardware-ops (for hardware-level ECC/unrecoverable errors).
- If maintenance involves vendor intervention, escalate to Vendor Partnerships (cc: infra-ops-lead).

Acceptance criteria for node re-introduction
- Node must show: no uncorrectable ECC events for 72 hours, driver_recovery_count < 1 in last 24h, and temps stable below 75C for 24 hours under 50th percentile load.
- A human sign-off by infra SRE is required for nodes that had ECC persistent or critical thermal events.

Migration notes and integration guidance
- When adding a new GPU type, the collector must ship a mapping and small calibration dataset that defines safe thresholds specific to the SKU. Calibration steps: run the canonical GPU stress harness for 4 hours at 70%-100% utilization and produce the p25/p50/p75 temp distribution. Attach mapping PR to telemetry repo.

Appendix A: Example mapping YAML snippet
# vendor -> canonical metric mapping (example)
# nvml collector mapping
collector_mappings:
  - vendor_metric: "nvml.temperature.gpu"
    canonical: "gpu.temp_celsius"
  - vendor_metric: "nvml.ecc.corrected"
    canonical: "gpu.ecc.corrected_count"
  - vendor_metric: "nvml.power.draw"
    canonical: "gpu.power_w"

Appendix B: Example incident timeline template
- detected_at: 2026-02-09T15:21:12Z
- detected_by: alert:gpu_vital_thermal_critical
- initial_metrics: {"temp_celsius": 92, "temp_climb_c_per_min": 12, "driver_recoveries": 0}
- remediation_start: 2026-02-09T15:23:00Z
- remediation_actions: ["reduce_concurrency", "graceful_drain"]
- drain_complete: 2026-02-09T15:26:00Z
- maintenance_ticket: GPU-3471
- postmortem_link: /confluence/postmortems/gpu-thermal-critical-2026-02-09
